Event Details

  • Date: 23 October 2026

  • Time: 4:00 PM – 5:30 PM

  • Venue: Basketball Court, I.T.S Engineering College, Greater Noida

  • Registration Fee: ₹300 per team

  • Prize Pool: ₹12,000

  • Team Size: 2 participants per team

  • Coordinator: Ms. Diksha Singh

Event Description

Welcome to Junior Robo Soccer at TechTrix'26, where robotics meets the excitement of football! Teams compete head-to-head using a custom-built, wirelessly controlled robot to maneuver a ball into the opponent's goal. Each team fields only one robot in the arena during a match. Control your robot, defend your goal, outplay your opponent, and score by getting the ball completely across the goal line.

Guidelines

1. Team & Robot Specifications

  • Team Size: 2 participants per team.

  • Maximum Dimensions: 350 × 350 mm (L × W).

  • Maximum Weight: 3 kg, including chassis, kicking mechanism, and batteries.

  • Maximum Voltage: 3S LiPo, 12V DC (3S, fully charged). IC engines, pneumatics, and compressors are prohibited.

  • Control: Fully wireless (RF or Bluetooth) manual control. Wired tethers are prohibited, and autonomous operation is strictly banned.

  • Ball Handling: At least 50% of the ball's surface must remain exposed at all times. Mechanisms that fully trap, grab, use suction on, or swallow the ball are prohibited.

  • Participants must bring their own robot, controller, and necessary spares.

2. School Participation Policy

  • Multiple teams from the same school or institution are permitted to participate.

  • Teams from the same school may share and use the same robot (bot), provided it meets all technical specifications and passes the technical inspection.

  • If two teams representing the same school reach the Semi-Finals and are scheduled to compete against each other, the school must decide which one of the two teams will proceed to the next round.

  • The school's decision must be communicated to the Event Coordinators before the Semi-Final match. The selected team will advance, while the other team will be eliminated from the competition.

  • This rule applies only when teams from the same school are matched against each other in the Semi-Finals. All other matches will proceed according to the announced knockout format.

  • The Event Organizers' decision regarding the implementation of this policy shall be final.

3. Pre-Event Inspection

  • Teams must report to the arena at least 30 minutes before the official start time.

  • Every robot will undergo a technical inspection and weigh-in.

  • Robots failing the weight, dimension, power, or ball-handling checks will be disqualified before the match begins.

4. Arena & Match Format

  • Arena: 8 ft × 4 ft, with 60 cm wide goalposts on each side.

  • Format: Single-elimination knockout, with byes assigned through a random draw in case of an uneven number of teams.

  • A standard match consists of two rounds of up to 90 seconds each.

  • The ball starts at the centre, with robots inside their respective defensive “D” areas until the referee's signal.

  • A goal is scored when the ball completely crosses the goal line.

  • A round is won by the first team to score. If neither team scores within 90 seconds, the round is declared a tie.

  • A team wins the match by winning both rounds, or by winning one round and tying the other.

  • A 30-second break is provided between rounds, during which teams switch sides.

  • If the ball goes out of bounds, play pauses, robots freeze in place, and the ball is reset to the centre.

  • If a robot completely stops working during a round, its team automatically forfeits that round. The robot may participate in the next round if repaired during the break.

  • An unsafe or uncontrollable robot may be removed from the match by the referee. The referee may also stop play for safety, ball recovery, or technical reasons.

5. Tie-Breaker

  • If the match is tied after two rounds, a third tie-breaker round of up to 90 seconds will be played. The first team to score wins.

  • If the third round also ends 0–0, the team with the fewest accumulated penalty points across all three rounds wins.

  • If both teams remain tied on goals and penalty points, the judges will decide the winner based on Aggression and Control.

6. Judging Criteria & Penalties

Penalties are tallied and used as tie-breakers; they do not result in free kicks.

  • Stalling (5-second rule): Holding, pinning, or trapping the ball in one position for more than 5 seconds — 1 penalty point.

  • Goal Camping (5-second rule): Parking entirely inside your own goal for more than 5 seconds without playing the ball — 1 penalty point.

  • Wall Pinning (5-second rule): Pinning the opponent against the arena wall while contesting the ball for more than 5 seconds — 1 penalty point.

  • Aggressive Ramming: Intentionally and repeatedly ramming the opponent instead of playing the ball — 1 penalty point.

  • Hand Touches: Manually resetting a flipped or stuck robot — 1 penalty point per touch.

7. Disqualification

The following actions will result in disqualification:

  • Exceeding the published dimensions, weight, or voltage limits.

  • Using a wired controller or autonomous operation.

  • Using ball-trapping or suction mechanisms that leave less than 50% of the ball exposed.

  • Deliberately damaging another team's robot.

  • Receiving unauthorized external assistance.

  • Poor social conduct, misbehaviour, foul or abusive language, or intentional damage to the arena or an opponent's robot.

8. Authority, Appeals & Final Decisions

The Event Jury, Referee, and Technical Committee hold final authority over match decisions, technical eligibility, penalties, disqualification, scoring, rule interpretation, and safety decisions.

Penalized teams may present their case to the Event Coordinators. However, the administration's verdict shall be final.

Important Note

Registration fees are non-refundable.
